theory.overview: Modern processors execute multiple threads simultaneously, requiring careful coordination to prevent race conditions and deadlocks. Understanding memory models, synchronization primitives, and lock-free algorithms is essential for writing correct and performant concurrent code.

keyConcepts.title: Memory Models
keyConcepts.content: Memory models define how threads observe each other's memory operations. Sequential consistency provides the strongest guarantees, while relaxed models allow reordering for performance but require explicit synchronization.

keyConcepts.title: Synchronization Primitives
keyConcepts.content: Mutexes provide mutual exclusion, condition variables enable waiting for conditions, semaphores control access to limited resources, and read-write locks allow multiple readers or one writer.

keyConcepts.title: Atomic Operations
keyConcepts.content: Atomic operations (compare-and-swap, fetch-and-add, etc.) provide lock-free synchronization. Memory orderings (relaxed, acquire, release, sequential) control visibility guarantees.

keyConcepts.title: Deadlock Prevention
keyConcepts.content: Deadlocks occur when threads circularly wait for resources. Prevention strategies: lock ordering (always acquire locks in the same order), lock timeout, deadlock detection, or lock-free algorithms.

steps.title: Thread Creation
steps.content: OS threads have their own stack and register state. Creating threads is expensive, so thread pools reuse threads for multiple tasks.

steps.title: Shared State Access
steps.content: When multiple threads access shared data, synchronization is needed. Locks provide safety but can cause contention. Atomic operations reduce contention for simple operations.

steps.title: Memory Ordering
steps.content: Compilers and CPUs reorder instructions for performance. Fences and atomic operations with proper memory ordering ensure visibility of writes across threads.

practiceProblems.title: Race Condition
practiceProblems.description: Two threads execute 'counter++' concurrently. Initial counter=0. What's the possible range?
practiceProblems.solution: Possible results: 1 or 2. If both read (0), both write (1), result is 1. If one completes before other starts, result is 2.

practiceProblems.title: Deadlock Detection
practiceProblems.description: Thread A locks X then Y. Thread B locks Y then X. What's the issue?
practiceProblems.solution: Potential deadlock. If A locks X and B locks Y, both wait forever. Fix: always acquire locks in consistent order (X before Y).

minigame.title: Race Condition Hunter
minigame.description: Identify and fix race conditions in concurrent code
